**Operator-window fix (LANDED, `b3de2f5d`):** Enter on `npm run ui` used to hand the operator
`refusing to open … a broker is driving it`, because `runOperatorWindow` spawned the WRITER while the
broker still owned the store. `stopBroker` is now a required step (record → STOP → spawn → release →
RESTART), proven end to end against a real broker on a temp store: ownership was `owned=true` before
Enter, free at the moment the session opened, and re-owned by a NEW broker pid after the window. The
attach contract (`<db>.attach.json`) is now gitignored (`975ef62a`).

**`npm run ui` → Enter (2026-10-22, operator-reported, FIXED in two landings).** Two separate failures,
both real, both proved on the live store:

1. `b3de2f5d` — the ruled operator window is record → **STOP** → acquire → session → release → RESTART,
   but `runOperatorWindow` only did spawn → release → restart, so `tui.mjs` (a WRITER) met the ownership
   guard and the operator got `refusing to open … a broker is driving it`. `stopBroker` is now a required
   step, wired in `src/tui/durable/enter.mjs`.
2. `f1246892` — the operator then got **`database is locked`**, from two causes: (a) `serve --stop`
   answering "no broker is running" is NOT proof the store is free — a previous window restarts the
   broker DETACHED, and for a moment there is no state file while that process opens the store; the stop
   now REPEATS and confirms with a real **writer open** (`probeWritable`). (b) the `ui.mjs` poller kept
   polling across the window, and with the broker gone it switches to `readLocal`, which opens the store
   and runs the WAL/pragma path — a second connection exactly when the child opens as a writer. The
   driver gained `pause()`/`resume()` (pause waits for the in-flight read and blocks new ones; resume
   repaints) and `ui.mjs` pauses around the window. `tui.mjs` opens with `busyTimeoutMs: 15_000`.
3. `bb55f7ce` — a BUSY rig needs more than one grace: with a seat generation in flight, `serve --stop`
   gives up after its 5 s grace, so the settle budget is now **30 s** (retries), overridable with
   `DURIG_WINDOW_SETTLE_MS`; past that the refusal NAMES the seat still generating, which is the
   actionable truth. `ui.mjs` prints one line before the freeze so a slow stop is not a mystery.

**Live proof** (`.spike/opwin-live.mjs`, real store, session spawn stubbed): broker up → Enter → stop →
`writerOpen=true` at spawn → release → broker restarted (new pid). And on a busy rig it refused in ~10 s

**1. The human queue — answered, not just relayed.** 10 rows sat on `deferredTo:"human"`; they were really
**5 questions**, 1 already answered by evidence, 1 a resume, and 6 stale liveness escalations from a dead `pm`.
Seven rulings (R1–R7) were delivered; the operator **accepted them in full**, which turned them into operator

unclaimable, so "registered" is not "will happen" — check the held bucket, not just the deferred one.

**2. Two landing + worktree passes (#3, #4): 11 branches landed, 10 terminal trees relocated, refs 95→88.**
`main` moved `f495091` → `66d0ce9` → `ee651e0`. Provenance and counts are in `land.md` / `branch-cleanup.md`
(dated entries) — read those, not this summary. Four traps were added there because they cost real landings:

- **A batch is ATOMIC and its `merged[]` is NOT a report** — it lists scratch merges whose `main` never moved.
- **`add/add` conflicts are order-independent** — two branches that both ADD a path can merge in NEITHER order;
  run the `diff --numstat` superset test and resolve to the superset (that is how `architect-item-3005` landed
  as `-rebased @328d838`).
- **`git cherry +` is not proof a branch is unique** — compare the TREES (`git diff main:<p> <b>:<p>`).
- **The suite can go red AND back green with no commit** — `npm install`/`npm ci` in the SHARED tree replaces the
  pinned `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-durable` symlink with the registry build (no `./codemode`), failing the
  five `tui-durable` demos. One-line check before trusting ANY suite verdict, in either direction:
  `ls -la node_modules/@earendil-works/ | grep pi-durable` (`->` pinned, `d` clobbered) → fix with
  `node scripts/sync-pi.mjs --link`.

**3. The worktree class has a CODE root cause, not just a doc gap.** A seat "asked about a worktree that no
longer existed"; then `impl` could not rebase `designer-item-2103` because a **locked** worktree over a
**cancelled** item held the branch. Reading `src/worktree.mjs` found the real defect: **the worktree PATH is
item-keyed (`item-<id>`) while the BRANCH is seat-keyed (`<seat>-item-<id>`), and reuse runs
`git checkout -B` unconditionally** — so a second seat preparing an item STEALS the first seat's worktree, and
nothing ever asks who holds a needed branch. Registered **`#3174`** (fix + refusals + failing-first demo) and
**`#3175`** (`lead`: item-keyed path vs seat-keyed branch is D110 territory). Hand-fix for today: free a held
branch with `git -C <holder> switch --detach` — never delete the worktree, never rebuild the branch.

**4. Two incident reports (both indexed):** `2026-10-19-terminal-worktree-mistaken-for-lost-work.md` (sev3, now
with the code root cause above) and `2026-10-19-git-sha-redacted-as-secret.md` (**sev2** — a bare 40-char git
SHA is classified `high-entropy-token` and redacted out of tool output; **confirmed live this session**: a
`devtools` call doing `git rev-parse HEAD` came back as a redaction marker). Consequence to remember: it
**blinds the landing tip-vs-pin gate** and can send the operator to rotate a credential that never existed.

## LANDED — broker liveness: re-wake per seat, not after the slowest run (delegate-owned; D65)

**Status: DONE.** `src/broker.mjs` `drivePass` waits only on the conversations a pass woke, races
that against the loop's commit signal, and `runWakeLoop` drains globally once on exit (F11);
`createWakeSignal` gained `race(promise)`; `PASS <n> ms=<dur> woke=<a,b>` is logged. Proof:
`demo/broker-liveness.test.mjs` (RED: 1 fast wake in 2 s → GREEN: 2nd wake ~27 ms in while the other
seat still generates). Commit `b81e171`. The narrative plan below is kept as the record of WHY.

**Why delegate-owned:** the fix is to the process that DRIVES the queue (the broker). A routed item
would sit behind the very broker it is meant to fix, so it must be done in the delegate seat directly
(code + tests + commit), then handed to the operator. The operator explicitly preferred this over the
durian-pi team for that reason.

### Symptom (observed 2026-10-16, pid 17424)

`<db>.broker.log`: `PASS 5` at `02:26:13`, its wakes fired, then **no `PASS 6` for 40+ min** (still
none at `03:10`). Measured pass intervals for this broker: 20.5, 20.3, 4.5, 27 min. Meanwhile `status`
showed **pm idle with 9 queued DONE-notices** and **qa idle with 2 queued artifacts**
(`idle_with_queued_work`), and a generation was live (genlock `scribe` since `03:10:05`). So seats with
queued work sat idle while a run was in flight.

### Root cause — what is VERIFIED vs INFERRED

**Verified (code + vendored contract):**

- `src/broker.mjs:146` (`drivePass`) calls `await harness.waitForIdle(context)` — the HARNESS method.
- Its contract (`node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-durable/dist/harness/types.d.ts:668-669`):

  > `Harness.waitForIdle` — “Resolve when the ordinary ownership scope of **every** ownerless
  > conversation has no live non-background task.”

  (A per-conversation wait exists too: `Conversation.waitForIdle`, line 87.)

- Therefore every pass blocks until **all** ownerless conversations are idle. And `src/scheduler.mjs`
  treats a submission settling as wake-relevant (“a submission settling … is exactly when a stalled
  claim becomes wakeable again”) — so the loop cannot act on that per-submission intent while parked in
  the global wait.
- **Code path (the decisive one):** `src/broker.mjs:258-274` does `await drivePass(...)` and THEN
  `passes++; logBrokerLine(dbPath, \`PASS ${passes}\`)`. So `PASS`is written **only after`drivePass`returns**, and`drivePass`returns **only after line 146's`harness.waitForIdle` resolves**, which is
  only when **every** ownerless conversation is idle. Consequence (a code-path FACT, not an inference):
  **no pass boundary — and therefore no next wake of ANY seat — until every in-flight run settles**; a
  seat that finished early is not re-woken until the slowest run finishes.

**UNVERIFIED (relative contribution):** how much of the 20–44-min pass time is this wait versus the
pass TAIL (`worktreeClaimed` cleanup, `supervise`). There is **no per-pass duration instrumentation**
(`grep -n 'Date.now() - |durationMs' src/broker.mjs` → none), so the split cannot be isolated without
adding it (the Observability step below) or a controlled experiment — and a controlled experiment is
blocked by the single-writer rule plus the running broker. **The mechanism is code-verified; only the
proportion is not.**

### The tool that exists to fix it

`Scheduler.waitForIdle(conversationId | undefined, context)` and `Conversation.waitForIdle(context)`
wait for **one** conversation (`harness/scheduler.d.ts:86`, `harness/types.d.ts:669`). The loop can
wait per-WOKEN-seat and re-wake others as they settle.

### The fix (chosen direction)

1. In `drivePass`, replace the single global `await harness.waitForIdle(context)` with a wait that
   settles when every conversation **this pass woke** is idle (track the woken conversation ids; wait
   on those only — do NOT wait on conversations this pass did not wake). A settle that the commit
   subscription raises should be able to end the wait early so the next pass starts promptly.
2. Preserve the F11 invariant that actually matters: **never close the harness with a live run**
   (keep it open while ANY run is in flight), rather than “wait for global idle”.
3. Leave the scheduler floor (`minIntervalMs = 500`) and per-seat cooldown
   (`SERVE_SEAT_COOLDOWN_MS = 30_000`) as-is; optionally lower the cooldown once passes are short.
4. Keep the per-pass `supervise`, but it must not gate the wake path.

### Observability (part of the fix)

- Log each pass with its DURATION and the seats it woke: `PASS <n> ms=<dur> woke=<a,b,c>`.
- Add a liveness notice/measure: “seat has queued work and **no live generation lease** for > N s” —
  distinct from the existing `idle_with_queued_work`, which cannot tell “waiting for the pass” from
  “wedged”. Surface in `status` and as a `check` rule.

### Tests (failing-first)

- **New `demo/broker-liveness.test.mjs`:** two seats; make one run long (faux provider with a delay /
  multi-turn script), give the other queued work; assert the second seat's wake appears in the broker
  log within a bound (≈5 s) **while the first is still running**. RED against the current
  global-`waitForIdle` broker; GREEN after the fix.
- Keep `broker.test.mjs`, `broker-max-duration`, `broker-cooperative-stop`, `broker-wakepath`,
  `broker-log`, `autostart` green; `node --check` clean; whole `demo/*.test.mjs` suite green.

### Acceptance

- A long run on one seat does NOT delay waking another seat with queued work (proven by the demo).
- Pass duration ≈ the pass's own work, not the longest run.
- Never closes the harness with a live run (no stranded submissions).
- `stop` / `serve --stop` / `--max-duration` semantics unchanged.

### Constraints / gotchas

- **Restart the broker to test the fix** — editing source does not affect the running process.
- Single-writer: only one `serve`/`run`/`send` at a time on `./selfdev.sqlite`.
- The tree may hold in-flight seat work (#623 etc.) — **stage explicit paths only**, never `git add -A`.
- Native Windows only; never push/publish.
- Related, lower priority: the **broker intent-inbox** (below) would let a delegate deliver intent
  without a `serve --stop`; and the worktree-leak defect (below) shares the same pass lifecycle.

## Pitfalls that slowed this session down (read before driving)

- **`run`/`serve --max-duration` is now a real bound (#429), but it was not** — a `--max-duration 300`
  broker ran >15 min. If you see that again, it is the defect, not your invocation.
- **`stop <seat>` aborts the run but leaves the `send` parent process alive.** `resume` finds nothing.
  After a `stop`, check for a lingering `node cli.mjs send ...` and `taskkill /F /PID` it. (Recorded
  lesson.)
- **A forced kill leaves a STALE genlock slot** (`.genlock.N`, dead pid) and the next driver may warn
  `held by pid <dead>` / `pid undefined` and stall. Check `selfdev.sqlite.genlock.*`; remove the ones
  whose pid is dead (they are lock files with no work).
- **A stop can also leave `cli.mjs serve --help`-style stray processes.** `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`
  filtered on `cli.mjs (send|run|serve)` is the fast check.
- **Seats thrash on hard native-interop work** (the P2-6 Job Object cost ~2 h across two abort/reset
  cycles). Give a bounded instruction; if the seat ignores it, `stop` + `reset <seat> <handoff>` and
  re-scope — do not let it run.
- **The broker/driver order is oldest-first per seat.** New priority items sit behind a 60-item
  backlog, so `claim_work({itemId})` via a direct `send <seat> --body-file` is the way to prioritize;
  grooming is the structural fix.
- **Two writers, precisely.** One _store/harness_ writer per DB (two `run`/`send` drivers race on the
  entry id, F24; `run`/`up` are not retried). Concurrency is `serve` + `DURIAN_PI_MAX_CONCURRENT_SEATS`.
  Per-task worktrees will make concurrent _editing_ safe once #473 lands.
- **Full suite > 120 s** so a single tool call times out; loop `demo/*.test.mjs` per file with a long
  timeout, or background it. Baseline is now **68/68** (the old `starter.test.mjs` CRLF failure is FIXED).
- **`edit` needs exact indentation and line endings.** The demo tests use 2-space indent; `src/rig.mjs`
  and others are CRLF. When a match misses, run `sed -n 'A,Bp' file | cat -A` before retrying.
- **Empty `catch {}` violates "errors are not swallowed"** and the warden flags it. Reporting it
  surfaced two real bugs in the broker demos (a scoped `broker` ReferenceError and `require` in ESM).
- **Seats clean up badly:** scratch appeared as `docs/WORKFLOWS.md.tmp`, `test.log`, and
  `undefined.broker.log`. The last one is a real bug: `src/broker.mjs` `brokerLogPath(dbPath)`
  returns `` `${dbPath}.broker.log` ``, so a falsy `dbPath` writes `undefined.broker.log` (it
  regenerates on a suite run). Guard against a falsy `dbPath` (no-op or throw). `git status` before
  every commit.
- **qa sometimes marks an item done while reporting it blocked** (#336/C4). Check the result text.

Last block I wrote in three documents that `metagpt` "has gone stale — pinned at 2026-01-21 while the other six are
2026-10-27/28". **Wrong.** `git -C vendor/eval/metagpt ls-remote origin HEAD` returns `11cdf466…` — that pin **is**
upstream's tip; the *project* is dormant, the *clone* is current. `node tools/vendor-pins.mjs --freshness` (new verb,
separate from `--check` on purpose: different question, needs the network, and its verdict implies an action) prints one
verdict word per clone. Measured 2026-10-28 on Linux, 7 clones, **10.3 s**, exit **1**:

```
CURRENT   metagpt 11cdf466 · symphony be10a1b7          ← dormant, not stale; a re-clone changes nothing
BEHIND    crewai f3d0099d→b95aa8bb · hermes-agent 07f075c2→5c668bbe · oh-my-pi 6f3fbc94→76772d0c
          openhands 6354932e→e4765e2c · prime-agent 815e64b5→ea9d9602      ← 5 of 7 moved within ONE day of cloning
```

`UNKNOWN` means upstream unread (offline) — **never infer dormant from it**. **No re-clone was performed:** a `BEHIND`
clone is re-vendored when a mechanism from it is about to be adopted, not on drift, because the reviews are valid against
their pins and re-pinning without re-reviewing destroys the evidence trail. If someone does re-clone, re-emit each

## Do not "fix" these on the strength of the docs

**An orphan-candidate verdict is not a release recommendation** — #725/#726/#727 have every cited gate `done` and are
*correctly* held by an operator clause; read the body (`stale-held-backlog.md` §Do). **A swept worktree ledger is not
"self-healing"** — on a moved workspace `git worktree prune` deletes evidence, and it runs unconditionally
(`src/broker.mjs:1167`); if `git worktree list` shrinks across your session, stop and write it down. **A suite that runs
"green" after files vanished is not green** — `scripts/suite.mjs:36` enumerates with `readdirSync(demoDir)`, so a deleted
member is a silent shrink, not a failure (233). **A `402` in a recent submission row is not current provider state** —
attribute it by joining to the first assistant entry after the admitted one (§Rig state, ROADMAP 226/229). **A `WAKE` in the preflight's
"after pass-1 reconcile" column is a prediction about reconcile**, not a delivered wake. **`queued` is not `claimable`**
in the queue sense: the queue's claimable state is `queued` *items*, and submission rows are a different table — mixing
them is how this session nearly mis-wrote 229. **`admissionVerdict` being inert means aged `queued` rows are never
withdrawn** — do not "recover" them by hand with a second writing Harness. `DURIG_MAX_CONCURRENT_SEATS` is unset in
`durig.config.json`, `"1"` in `durig.config.default.json`, and the observed profile is **not** single-flight (max 11 in
flight) — read `src/config.mjs loadConfig` first (D153 §4). The 5-minute degeneration bound is a *turn* guard on a
different quantity, and the 5-minute **admission** deadline is a different 5 minutes again. A `--dry-run` names no
removals (resets model+cwd only) — not a safety check. Model speed is **12.7%** of machine time. `tools/` is untested by
design except where a demo is named. **A `single-model-rig` PASS is not certification** — it compares model *strings*
(**D137**); the seeded-bug gate is the certification. **An empty answer from a reasoning model at a small `max_tokens` is
a budget artifact, not a dead model** (flint: 750 of 803 completion tokens were reasoning; the same call at 8 tokens
returns `finish_reason: stop` with empty content), and **`TRUNCATED-EMPTY` rows measure the output budget as much as the
model** — read the run's budget before reading its verdict. **A model server's `loaded_instances` entry is not a health
check**: the zombie that started this session listed flint loaded at 262,144 while every request 400'd.

## Do not "fix" these on the strength of the docs

**`fetch failed` from a probe is a transport ceiling, not a dead model or an out-of-RAM box** — compute
`budget_tok ÷ measured_tok_per_s` against 300 s (probes) and 600 s (the rig's SDK) and print `err.cause` (**254**, D164).
**A `TRUNCATED-EMPTY` verdict measures the output budget as much as the model** — read the run's budget and the model's
reasoning shape first; flint emits **0 answer chars** at 1,200 and at 4,000 tokens, so no budget tuning fixes it.
**`1/1 scored` is not a capability rate** — in the completed run 19 of 24 prompts never reached `finish=stop`, so the
flattering denominator is an artifact of the print, not a result (**257**). **A control-side `FALSE-ALARM` may be our
feeding, not the model** — two of them claimed missing imports on a fragment whose import block the window had cut off;
**195**'s excuser saw the class and excused 0. **Decode is not a constant**: 42.21 tok/s isolated vs **21.8–48.9 tok/s
(p50 35)** inside one run, with `strata-host` at 100 % on the other GPU — budget off the low end, and **a model speed claim
is a claim about a quantization** (**255** acceptance (5)). **A model key does not identify a model** — verify the live
`.gguf` with `ps -eo args | grep llama-server`. **An unreachable commit is somebody's work, not garbage** — `git gc`
deletes it (cross-clone runbook). **A `single-model-rig` PASS is not certification** (**D137**). **`reapable: 0` in
`worktree audit` is not a verdict** (`docs/BRANCH-AND-WORKTREE-LIFECYCLE.md:244`). **0 claimable rows means a started team
idles or improvises.** **An orphan-candidate verdict is not a release recommendation** (#725/#726/#727 are *correctly*
held). **A swept worktree ledger is not "self-healing"** (`src/broker.mjs:1167`). **A suite that runs green after files
vanished is not green** (`scripts/suite.mjs:36`). **A `402` in a recent row is not current provider state.** **A `WAKE` in
the preflight's post-pass-1 column is a prediction.** **`queued` (submissions) ≠ `queued` (claimable items).**
**`DURIG_MAX_CONCURRENT_SEATS` is unset in `durig.config.json`, `"1"` in the default — read `src/config.mjs loadConfig`
(D153 §4).** **A `--dry-run` names no removals.** **Model speed is 12.7% of machine time.** **A loaded_instances entry is
not a health check.** **Never quote your own shas in
a pointer.**

## Do not "fix" these on the strength of the docs

**A probe that sends no system message is measuring the HOST, not the model** — this LM Studio injects *"think… as long as you
want"* when none is sent (arms A–D in the notes; retained body `.spike/gate/ministral-probe.json`: 600/600 tokens, 599
reasoning, `content=0ch`; a bounding system message → 1.9 s / 62 tokens / correct; four reasoning toggles do nothing) (**259**).
**A model that answers quickly is not verifying** — ministral: 24/24 answers, 16/16 clean controls wrong. **`TRUNCATED-EMPTY`
conflates "budget too small" with "generation degenerated into a loop"**, and **a `ctx-size` you did not read from the process
table is a guess**; a declared `_CONTEXT` above the served one makes the request unsatisfiable (**259**). **Never start a probe
arm without printing available RAM, swap used and per-GPU MiB** — my arms helped OOM-kill the seats' server on 2026-10-29.
**`fetch failed` from a probe is a transport ceiling, not a dead model or an out-of-RAM box** — compute
`budget_tok ÷ measured_tok_per_s` against 300 s (probes) and 600 s (the rig's SDK) and print `err.cause` (**254**, D164).
**`1/1 scored` is not a capability rate** — in the completed run 19 of 24 prompts never reached `finish=stop`, so the
flattering denominator is an artifact of the print, not a result (**257**). **A control-side `FALSE-ALARM` may be our
feeding, not the model** — **three of flint's four** claimed missing imports on a fragment whose import block my window had
cut off; **195**'s excuser saw the class and excused 0. **Decode is not a constant**: 42.21 tok/s isolated vs **21.8–48.9 tok/s
(p50 35)** inside one run, with `strata-host` at 100 % on the other GPU — budget off the low end, and **a model speed claim
is a claim about a quantization** (**255** acceptance (5)). **A model key does not identify a model** — verify the live
`.gguf` with `ps -eo args | grep llama-server`. **An unreachable commit is somebody's work, not garbage** — `git gc`
deletes it (cross-clone runbook). **A `single-model-rig` PASS is not certification** (**D137**). **`reapable: 0` in
`worktree audit` is not a verdict** (`docs/BRANCH-AND-WORKTREE-LIFECYCLE.md:244`). **0 claimable rows means a started team
idles or improvises.** **An orphan-candidate verdict is not a release recommendation** (#725/#726/#727 are *correctly*
held). **A swept worktree ledger is not "self-healing"** (`src/broker.mjs:1167`). **A suite that runs green after files
vanished is not green** (`scripts/suite.mjs:36`). **A `402` in a recent row is not current provider state.** **A `WAKE` in
the preflight's post-pass-1 column is a prediction.** **`queued` (submissions) ≠ `queued` (claimable items).**
**`DURIG_MAX_CONCURRENT_SEATS` is unset in `durig.config.json`, `"1"` in the default — read `src/config.mjs loadConfig`
(D153 §4).** **A `--dry-run` names no removals.** **Model speed is 12.7% of machine time.** **A loaded_instances entry is
not a health check.** **Never quote your own shas in
a pointer.**

## Do not "fix" these on the strength of the docs

**A `BLOCK seat-shell-availability` is not advice to start anyway** — and it is not proof the *whole* start is unsafe
(`pm` needs no shell): name the exception, do not bypass the guard. **Seat hygiene is currently UNMEASURED**, not good —
**20,340** `powershell` calls are the Windows era and **0** `bash` rows mean no seat has ever run `git` here. **A
`documents.kind` value is JSON-quoted** (`WHERE kind='durig.queue'` returns nothing) **and the queue payload lives in
`document_revisions` deltas** — read queue state through `cli.mjs queue` / `tools/roadmap-queue-coverage.mjs`, never a
hand-rolled query. **`--dry-run`'s finding count moves for real reasons** (provider-probe transience; `live-tree-dirty`
while the delegate's own edits are uncommitted) — **re-run before reporting**, and **it never names a removal**. **A model key
does not identify a model** — verify the live `.gguf` with `ps -eo args | grep llama-server`, and **an `ctx-size` you never
read off the process table is a guess**. **A probe that sends no system message measures the HOST, not the model** (**259**).
**A model that answers quickly is not verifying** — ministral 24/24 answers, 16/16 clean controls wrong.
**`TRUNCATED-EMPTY` conflates "budget too small" with "generation degenerated"**. **Never start a probe arm
without printing available RAM, swap used and per-GPU MiB** — my arms helped OOM-kill the seats' server. **`fetch failed`
from a probe is a transport ceiling, not a dead model** — compute `budget_tok ÷ tok/s` against 300 s (probes) / 600 s (the
SDK) and print `err.cause` (**254**). **`1/1 scored` is not a capability rate** (**257**). **A control-side `FALSE-ALARM` may
be our feeding, not the model** (**195**). **Decode is not a constant** (42.2 tok/s isolated vs 21.8–48.9 in-run) — budget off
the low end, and **a speed claim is a claim about a quantization** (**255**). **An unreachable commit is somebody's work.** **A `single-model-rig` PASS is not certification** (**D137**). **`reapable: 0` is
not a verdict**, and **a swept worktree ledger is not "self-healing"** (`src/broker.mjs:1167`). **A suite that runs green
after files vanished is not green** (`scripts/suite.mjs:36`). **A `402` in a recent row is not current provider state**, and
**`queued` (submissions) ≠ `queued` (claimable items)**. **An orphan-candidate verdict is not a release recommendation**
(#725/#726/#727 are *correctly* held). **A promoted instrument is "cited but untracked" until you stage it.** **Never quote shas.**

## Do not "fix" these on the strength of the docs

**A `BLOCK seat-shell-availability` is not advice to bypass it** — but it is also not proof the start is unsafe: check
whether the finding is *computing* anything. `--ack-coordinator-wake` currently never can (the `op === "?"` filter above).
**A broker start is not coordinator-scoped just because you addressed coordinators** — the queue's claimable head decides
who wakes. **`pause` is rig-level**; there is no per-seat gate. **"Coordinator" is a capability verdict, not a seat name** —
`review` and `security` keep the shell. **A `--refresh` without `DURIG_SEAT_ROOT` exported repairs nothing about the root**
(it writes `cwd` only when defined, `cli.mjs:679`), and `--refresh` is all-12 at once and applies model resets you did not
ask for — read its `wouldReset`. **`vendor/pi-main` is gitignored, so a new worktree has none**: copy the built one
(723 MB, 2 s) and run `sync-pi --link` rather than rebuilding the pin; `npm ci --prefer-offline` is 4.4 s offline, not the
~12 s quoted in the code comment. **`git status` cannot see `.durig/` leaks** at any depth; scan the filesystem by name.
**A `--dry-run` that names no removals is not evidence there are none.** **Never read an exit code through a pipe.**
**A promoted instrument is "cited but untracked" until you stage it.** **Append to a growing file with `>>`; never rewrite a
file from its own contents** (D170) — and **diff names, not counts**. **Never quote shas.**

**A provider that answers a 26-token probe is not healthy** — probe with a *real request size*; and now: **a 200 at 9,627 tokens is still
not a working verifier** — the leg lives or dies on role *sequence*, not size. **`reset <seat> <handoff>` appends a user turn** →
`system, user, user` → a strict template answers 500 in ~30 ms with zero tokens. **An errored turn leaves its user message in the
conversation**, so the next attempt is structurally inadmissible and the poison grows monotonically (qa: 193 errored turns, 1 answer).
**`compact` writing no entry is not a window problem.** **Never treat "the free GPU" as the one you think** — the local model owns GPU1.
**`pgrep -f "cli.mjs send …"` matches the shell that asked** — test the process line or the JSON's `stopReason`. **Running any instrument
inside a worktree silently changes the rig it measures** — the seat root now has a config with an absolute `DURIG_DB`, so pin `DURIG_DB`
to a scratch store before running the suite there. **The portability audit is blind to the `complete_work` root decay** (#4884 is the
carrier). **`complete_work` re-points a seat's persisted cwd to `process.cwd()`** — never treat a re-point as durable before #4882.
**A `--dry-run` that names no removals is not evidence there are none.** **Never read an exit code through a pipe.** **Append prose with a
quoted heredoc + `cat >>`, not `printf`.** **A promoted instrument is "cited but untracked" until you stage it.** **Never quote shas.**
**LM Studio's GGUF stores each KV value's type as a 4-byte field** — a 1-byte reader desyncs by 3 bytes (`.spike/gguf-arch.mjs`).

## Do not "fix" these on the strength of the docs

**A verifier that reads a 26 KB file whole loses the turn to its own compaction** (`seatguard.mjs` is 26,532 chars;
the dead band is `input ≳ 20,000` on a 24,576 window). **Auto-compaction CAN fire near the ceiling and then write a
summary that keeps the newest 20,000 tokens anyway** — "it never fires" is D175's error, re-measured 2026-10-30.
**A completed verify row can carry citations that point nowhere, and `review-cite-check.mjs` exits 0 on them** — it
checks existence and range, not content. **A seat's `complete_work` moves its persisted cwd to the serving process's
cwd** — run your `send` from the approved root and re-check with `up … --refresh --dry-run` (F12 then fails closed).
**An errored or length-cut turn leaves its user message and an empty assistant message in the conversation**; a bare
`reset` is what the shape defect makes the cure, and it costs the seat its context. **A provider that answers a
26-token probe is not healthy.** **`send` printing `DEPRECATED` is not a reason to start a broker.** **LM Studio
restores `--ctx-size 8192 --parallel 4` on app relaunch; its `--estimate-only` runs ~0.35 GiB low.** **`pgrep -f
"cli.mjs send …"` matches the shell that asked.** **Running any instrument inside a worktree silently changes the rig
it measures** — pin `DURIG_DB` to a scratch store there. **The portability audit's answer depends on which tree it
runs from** (#4895). **A `--dry-run` that names no removals is not evidence there are none.** **Never read an exit
code through a pipe.** **Append prose with a quoted heredoc + `cat >>`, never `printf`, and never put backticks
inside `git commit -m "…"` — use `-F <file>`.** **Run prettier only on the paths you authored, and NEVER on
`docs/NEXT-ARCHIVE.md` or a durable record you are appending to.** Measured this session: `npx prettier --write` on the
archive reflowed **976 diff lines of pre-existing verbatim prose** (`*word*` → `_word_`, hard-wrap, blank line after
every heading) and silently broke the "cut verbatim" claim — restore with `git show HEAD:<file> > <file>` and re-append.
`demo/format.test.mjs` does **not** gate repo-wide formatting: its own header says the format verb is
"explicit-paths-only and never a tree walk or a hook", and `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/NEXT-ARCHIVE.md` and both
verifier runbooks are **unformatted at HEAD** (checked with `prettier --check`).
**`compact` cannot rescue a seat at its ceiling — it IS a summarization call and fails for the same reason the turn
failed** (pm 184,507/200,000: `Summarization hit the token limit`; qa2 at 18,453/24,576: `no compaction entry was
written`). **`resume`/`doctor` CANCELS a `placed` run, it does not retry it** (`cli.mjs:1101-1112`: `already_placed` →
`conv.abort()`), and it is a compound write. **`cli.mjs <verb> --help` RUNS THE VERB** — there is no per-verb help; the
delegate's `doctor --help` performed a real cancel (benign here, logged in D177). **A backgrounded seat run dies with
the harness unless it is detached with `setsid`** — tonight the delegate's session died mid-`send`, the child died with
it, and lead's submission was left `placed` (the brief itself survived in the conversation). **The host is out of RAM

## Do not "fix" these on the strength of the docs

**A seat's shell WORKS in its own item worktree and REFUSES in the shared checkout — do not "fix" the refusal.** The
guard's degraded-cwd rule is correct and 217's own demo proves it (`ok #3992: a shell command from a seat's OWN worktree
is NOT refused`). To get any seat-executed act you need a **claimed row** first: `prepare_workspace` refuses without one
(`no claimed item #NNNN is yours`), and its **default** re-attaches to the most recently claimed item — pass the itemId
explicitly or you land in someone else's worktree. **`up … --refresh --dry-run`
printing `changes: {}` is not evidence about the seat root** when the rig file names no cwd. **A seat's `complete_work`
moves its persisted cwd to the serving process's cwd** — run `send` with **cwd = the approved seat root**, and NEVER unset
`DURIG_SEAT_ROOT` to get past a drift refusal: that is how a seat gets served from a **different checkout** (D180).
**`status.attention` never lists a seat whose `context` fraction
exceeds 1** (measured: `advocate` 9.96, `architect` 1.09, both absent) — compute reachability from `status.context`
before every wake. **A `DONE` verify row can cite lines that point nowhere and `review-cite-check.mjs` exits 0 on them.**
**Auto-compaction fires late, not never** (D176/D177), and **`compact` cannot rescue a seat at its ceiling**. **Never read
an exit code through a pipe.** **A `--dry-run` that names no removals is not evidence there are none.** **A backgrounded
seat run dies with the harness unless detached with `setsid`.** **`cli.mjs <verb> --help` RUNS the verb; `resume`/
`doctor` CANCELS a `placed` run.** **Pin `DURIG_DB` — running an instrument inside a worktree silently changes the rig
it measures.** **A FRESH worktree has no gitignored `durig.config.json`, so a suite sweep run there returns a FALSE
RED** (#4895 tree-class). **Append prose with a quoted heredoc or `cat file >>`, never `printf`; never put backticks in
`git commit -m` — use `-F <file>`.** **Run prettier only on paths you authored, NEVER on `docs/NEXT-ARCHIVE.md` or a
durable record you are appending to.** **LM Studio restores `8192×4` on relaunch.**

## Do not "fix" these on the strength of the docs

**A dead provider is not a shape defect and not a seat defect** — probe at the failing size, read `--ctx-size` in `ps`,
and compare against `DURIG_VERIFIER_CONTEXT` before blaming a seat (this session burned three turns learning it).
**Raising GPU capacity is the operator's spend.** **`send` reporting `done` proves nothing** — read `stopReason`
(`length` = capacity, `error`/`model_error` = refused, and 6,128 input tokens already leaves no room to answer).
**A seat's shell WORKS in its own item worktree and REFUSES in the shared checkout — do not "fix" the refusal.** Any
seat-executed act needs a **claimed row** first; `prepare_workspace` refuses without one and its **default** re-attaches to
the most recently claimed item — **pass the itemId explicitly**. **`up … --refresh --dry-run` printing `changes: {}` is
VACUOUS**; **never unset `DURIG_SEAT_ROOT` to get past a drift refusal** (D180: that is how a seat gets served from a
different checkout and leaves a nested worktree); **a seat's `complete_work` moves its persisted cwd to the serving
process's cwd**, so serve from the approved root. **`status.attention` never lists a seat whose `context` fraction
exceeds 1.** **A `DONE` verify row can cite lines that point nowhere and `review-cite-check.mjs` exits 0 on them.**
**Auto-compaction fires late, not never**, and **`compact` cannot rescue a seat at its ceiling**. **Never read an exit
code through a pipe**; **`> /dev/null` is refused** (#4924) — redirect into your own worktree. **A `--dry-run` that names
no removals is not evidence there are none.** **A backgrounded seat run dies with the harness unless `setsid`.**
**`cli.mjs <verb> --help` RUNS the verb; `resume`/`doctor` CANCELS a `placed` run.** **Pin `DURIG_DB` — running an
instrument inside a worktree silently changes the rig it measures.** **A FRESH worktree has no gitignored
`durig.config.json` and its deps are not linked, so a suite run there is a FALSE RED** (#4915: `DEPENDENCY NOT LINKED`;
`Durable SQLite schema version 2 … newer than supported version 1`; 80 vs 187 packages). **The redactor eats 40-hex
tokens — including pinned patch-ids inside a row body — so assert shas by computing the comparison inside the shell and
reporting halves** (#4922). **Backticks in a shell-written brief are eaten.** **Append prose with a quoted heredoc or
`cat file >>`, never `printf`; never put backticks in `git commit -m` — use `-F <file>`.** **Run prettier only on paths
you authored, NEVER on `docs/NEXT-ARCHIVE.md` or a durable record you are appending to.** **LM Studio restores
`8192×4` on relaunch.**

## 7. The DeepInfra backup verifier — what the instruments say before anyone spends (operator asked; delegate measured, chose nothing)

Rawest material, fetched keyless this session: `curl -s https://api.deepinfra.com/v1/models` → `http=200`, **173 models**,
saved at `.spike/delegate-20261102/deepinfra-models.json` (the operator's docs page is the same list, prettier). Prices
below are that file's `metadata.pricing` (`$ per Mtok in/out`), and the per-turn column uses **this rig's own** verifier
prompt shape — p50 **55,538** / max **108,435** input tokens, cited from commit `ecdeb70f`, × 3,000 output
(`DURIG_VERIFIER_MAX_TOKENS`):

| candidate | $in / $out | ctx | cost per verify turn (p50) | in the curated catalog `buildModels` reads? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-Turbo` | 0.02 / 0.04 | 131,072 | **$0.0012** | no |
| `openai/gpt-oss-20b` (reasoning) | 0.03 / 0.14 | 131,072 | $0.0021 | no |
| **`openai/gpt-oss-120b`** (reasoning) | 0.037 / 0.17 | 131,072 | **$0.0026** | **no** |
| **`google/gemma-3-4b-it`** | 0.05 / 0.10 | 131,072 | $0.0031 | **no** |
| **`mistralai/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506`** | 0.075 / 0.20 | 128,000 | **$0.0048** | **YES — the only one of the four** |
| **`google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`** (reasoning) | 0.07 / 0.34 | 262,144 | $0.0049 | **no** |
| `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (reasoning, `prompt_cache`) | live 0.060 / 0.18 | 1,048,576 | $0.0039 | yes, at **0.09/0.18** — a stale price |

**"Lowest price" is the wrong lever here, and the arithmetic is the reason.** The whole credible band is **$0.0012–$0.0049 per
turn** — a 30-turn verify evening is **$0.04 to $0.15**. The gap between the cheapest 8B model and a 120B reasoning model is
**a third of a cent per turn**. Spending the gate's real cost (a `gate.mjs` run with clean controls, k≥3) is orders of
magnitude more expensive than the model choice, so qualify first and price-tie-break second.

Three hard filters the rig imposes, all measured, none of them price:
1. **ctx ≥ 128k.** Verifier prompts run p50 55.5k / max 108.4k. `DURIG_VERIFIER_CONTEXT` is declared **24,576** — below the
   p50, the impossible pair D166 registered as **259**, still unfixed. Any DeepInfra row must set ctx honestly or the swap
   just moves the failure.
2. **Tool calling.** `rig.selfdev.json` gives the five verifier seats **no `tools` restriction**, so a verify leg runs the seat
   loop with tools; the live catalog's `tags` do not state function-calling support for any candidate. Must be probed per
   model, not assumed from the spec sheet.
3. **A bounded system message.** D166 measured that requests without one inherit the host's "be as long as you want"
   instruction and die at `finish=length`. That is host-side for LM Studio; a remote provider needs the same bounding
   asserted, or the p50 becomes the budget instead of the prompt.

And the substrate gap that decides the ordering: `src/providers/deepinfra-models.ts` `fallbackModels()` (16 entries) is what
`buildModels` reads, and `fetchDeepInfraModels` (line 130) is imported nowhere — the test header says so. So three of the
operator's four candidates resolve to **`no_model` before a request is made**, which is the 2026-10-19 outage class. Also
**`mistralai/ministral-3-14b-reasoning` is not in the live DeepInfra catalog at all** — so §0a's fix must not "fix" the guard
by adding it. Finally: **there is no spend cap and no cost ledger anywhere** (`grep -nE "SPEND|BUDGET|CAP_" src/config.mjs` →
nothing; `grep -rn MAX_SPEND_USD src/*.mjs cli.mjs` → nothing; no `src/costsheet.mjs`) while `docs/SELFDEV.md` §0 asserts
"hard caps and the cost recorded". Write the cap before pointing five seats at a metered API.

**What the delegate needs from the operator to go further:** (a) `DEEPINFRA_API_KEY` in the *environment*, never in
`durig.config.json` (`src/config.mjs:31,106` records a key that leaked there once); (b) a ruling that amends D137's model
clause — a remote verifier is a *different engine*, which is a genuine independence gain over the single-family local rig,
but only if reports keep saying which independence they actually got; (c) whether to pay for the qualification run
(`node tools/model-probes/gate.mjs https://api.deepinfra.com/v1/openai <model> <label> --replicate 3 --plan` first, spend
nothing, then the paid arm). Recommended shortlist for that run: `gpt-oss-120b` (reasoning, cheapest reasoning-capable),
`Mistral-Small-3.2-24B` (zero substrate change), `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (1M ctx + prompt cache, and at 55k re-sent prefix
the cache may beat headline price — D147 measured 8,757 cached tokens in 96 ms warm).

### 1b. THE NEW RED — `demo/seat-turn-shape.test.mjs:292` is red for any store with a non-empty WAL (A/B, mechanism named)

Failure: `AssertionError: the read must not modify …/selfdev.sqlite` — the demo hashes the live store before and after
`readSeatShapes`, and its own connection changed the bytes.

    cp selfdev.sqlite{,-wal} .spike/…/store-copy.sqlite{,-wal} (wal 2,912,872 B) → DURIG_DB=copy node demo/seat-turn-shape.test.mjs
    exits 1; afterwards the copy's -wal is GONE and its db sha changed a40b7304 → 3e3d6931, with no other writer present

Mechanism: the reader opens the store **read-write**, so SQLite replays/truncates the WAL on open, which rewrites the db file
the demo is hashing. So the guard is **red whenever the WAL is non-empty** (the normal state after any write) and green only
when the WAL happens to be empty — a lottery member, the same shape as #4995/#4996, passing until now by luck.
**Blast radius, measured:** `node tools/what-to-test.mjs --no-scan --paths=src/readapi.mjs,demo/seat-turn-shape.test.mjs`
→ **derived guards: 9 test(s) — 9 direct + 0 family mention**, so every `src/readapi.mjs` landing inherits the member.
Fix direction handed to the seat, not chosen by the delegate: assert what the read proves without asserting file immutability
(open read-only, digest the read result, or name the WAL state). `lead`'s ruling put the fix in **product** (`src/readapi.mjs`,
a read-only open) as **#5019 → impl**, the demo forced to **construct** a non-empty WAL; **"flaky" is banned as a label**.

### 2. THE BLOCKER — a summarization OUTPUT cap, named at the lines (it is neither the Jinja alternation nor a window)

`thresholdCompaction` (`vendor/pi-main/packages/durable/dist/harness/generation.js`) fires when
`estimateContext(view, planned) > contextWindow − policy.reserveTokens`. durian-pi sets **no** compaction policy, so the pinned
defaults apply: `reserveTokens 16384, keepRecentTokens 20000, backgroundTokens 32768` (`harness/agent.js:10-15`). With
`DURIG_LOCAL_CONTEXT=160000` the band is **143,616**. Measured `status.context.consumed`: `lead` **145,429** (over at rest),
`devtools` **143,426** (190 under at rest), `impl` **143,278** (338 under) — and the check counts the **appended send**, so a brief
pushes all three over. The summary request's output budget is `min(0.8·16384, model.maxTokens)` = `min(13,107, 8,192)` because
`DURIG_LOCAL_MAX_TOKENS` is unset and defaults to **8,192** (`harness/compaction.js:95`; `src/providers/local.mjs:76,85`). At that cap
the summarizer returns `stopReason=length` → `summaryFailure` prints exactly *“Summarization hit the token limit; the summary is
incomplete”* (`compaction.js:302-303`) → `failModelError` settles the **whole send** `unanswered/model_error`, zero tokens.
**Consequence for #4970:** the declared window is not cosmetic drift — it **is** the trigger. 200,000 moves the band to **183,616** and
all three seats fall under it, with the engine already serving 204,800 (`ps` command line + `tools/model-probes/probe-preflight.mjs`:
window 204800, strata 51.2 GiB RSS, `gpus:[0,1]`). **Still not hand-aligned**: D195's ruling stands (aligning by hand is drift with
better numbers; the fix is one source of truth). Rows in this class, none built: **#4973** (held, gated on #4970 — `pm` judges the
input-bound half capacity-independent, carried in **#5028**), **#4887** (queued — no policy knob exists to set), **#4964** (held),
**#4981** (queued; `pm` routes it as legibility, **#5029**, not gated on capacity).

The server on `127.0.0.1:47831` demands a key, and `src/providers/local.mjs` sent `LOOPBACK_PLACEHOLDER_KEY`, so all
seven `local/iq3_s` seats failed `401`. **Fixed:** key in `~/.config/durig/env` (600, outside the repo), loaded with

`cli.mjs config` prints **0** occurrences of the value; `secretFindings: []`. **Never** put a key in
`durig.config.json` — gitignored still means *inside the tree*. LAN share: `0.0.0.0:47832` inference-only, `200`
with a bearer token; **`--permanent --list-ports` lists neither port**, so a `firewall-cmd --reload` or reboot closes
it — `sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=47832/tcp && sudo firewall-cmd --reload` to keep it. **Trap:** a
same-host test through your own LAN IP passes for any port (own-address traffic loops over `lo`); only
`--query-port`/`--list-all` or a second machine answers a firewall question. `tools/broker-serve.mjs:228` probes
`/v1/models` **without** a credential while `:255` sends one → a working provider reads as `unreachable: HTTP 401`

## Traps this session found (mirrored into `docs/SELFDEV.md` §sessions E–F)

1. **`no_model` is a store failure, not a config failure.** `check`, the pointer demo and the roster all stayed green while
   11 seats died at wake. The only signal was inside the task record. Probe: `up --refresh --dry-run` →
   `wouldRefresh[].changes.model = {from,to}` (299).
2. **`up --refresh` is the fix verb and it is not free** — one `pi.reset` per seat. And it **refuses while a resident broker
   owns the store**: stop the broker first, or route through `intent.mjs`.
3. **A CLI verb that re-registers the catalog needs the env file.** Run `resume`/`up` without
   `--env-file="$HOME/.config/durig/env"` and the verifier family prints `registration-refused …
   metered-endpoint-unkeyed` — I reproduced this twice (D215, 299).
4. **Store values are JSON-encoded.** `kind`/`status` compare against `'"pi.agent"'`, `entries` has no top-level
   `kind`/`at`, and there is no `items`/`seats` table. Hand-written SQL from memory burns time — use
   `tools/latency-budget.mjs`, `cli.mjs status`, `cli.mjs queue`.
5. **`.spike/serve.out` accumulates every run.** Parse the **last** block; a whole-file regex reported an old run's
   `passes=1245` as the current one's result and nearly wrote a false number into this file.
6. **`cli.mjs log <seat>` can hang to timeout while the broker is mid-turn** (exit 124, no output).

`Type.Object({}, {additionalProperties: true})` sites need `{ open: true }`); `documentState` → `snapshot`, which
returns the **value**, not a wrapper; `watchEvents` → `src/livewatch.mjs` `watchLive()`; `subscribeCommits` →
`src/commitstream.mjs` `followCommits()` over `Session.observeCommits`; `Storage.commit(batches, receive, ctx)`;
and `checkpointWhen: () => false` on the 6 rig docs, **provisional** (ROADMAP 355, rows #6171–#6173). Both seams are
documented as approximations: turn boundaries come from the generation attempt, not a turn record; tool results are
synthesised from committed `pi.tool-result` entries, not streamed.

**What the cleanup left** (re-measured at `f3ffce0e`, `cli.mjs worktree audit --json`, 1.1 s) — 25 worktrees, **0 locked**:
7 seat roots + 1 non-item, **4 live** rows (`item-1158` claimed, `item-3087` claimed dirty 2, `item-5912` held, `item-6177`
claimed dirty 3), **17 reapable**, and **4 dirty orphans** whose items are `done`: `item-6057`
(2 tracked edits — a `sync-pi --no-repair` flag and its demo, **not on `main`**: `grep -c "no-repair" scripts/sync-pi.mjs`
→ 0, while `git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/heads/item-6057 refs/heads/main` exits 0, i.e. the branch is merged and
the work is not), `item-6290` (23 untracked solo-run logs, 45 KB), `item-6317` (3 logs), `item-6328` (1 log). Every
residue is exported to `.spike/worktree-residue/` (gitignored, 148 KB) before anything is touched. A dirty orphan is
refused on purpose: a seat commits it, or the operator rules it discarded.

**The recipe that made this fast (re-run it, it is idempotent):**

```bash
DURIG_DB=./selfdev.sqlite node cli.mjs worktree audit --json > .spike/wt.json
node -e 'const j=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(".spike/wt.json","utf8"));
 for(const w of j.worktrees) if(w.keepReason==="reapable") console.log(w.worktree)' | while read -r p; do git worktree remove "$p"; done   # 75 s for 57 trees, never --force
git worktree prune
```

**Goal: implementation complete — the audit's two objections are closed; completion re-requested.** "Every CLI verb
answers or fails fast against a team running or stopped, no 120 s silence, and Ctrl-C actually terminates the verb."
All legs are on `main`: the signal seam (`src/signals.mjs`, `src/cli-seam.mjs`), bounded reads (`src/readclient.mjs`),
the read-only shim (`src/readonlystore.mjs`), the out-of-band read drain in `runWakeLoop`, the **mutating-verb** bound
(`intentWaitBoundMs`, `src/broker.mjs:2422`: 900 s advancing / 10 s frozen pass / 0 no broker — `cli.mjs pause --wait`
against a 658 MB store with no resident broker answered in **349 ms**), and the stop-receipt legs (`src/broker.mjs:1851`,
`:1889`, `:2192`). Re-measured 08:1xZ, broker resident: `status --json` 10.1 s, `queue --json --no-body` 2.0 s, `watch --once --json` 1.9 s,
`ps` 0.5 s, unknown verb `verify --json` exit 2 in 304 ms. Objection 1 (NEXT.md over the cap) is closed — 197 lines, the
pointer test green. Objection 2 (mutating verbs defaulting to 15 min) is closed — `cli.mjs:2008` defaults `timeoutMs = null`
and derives the bound from `intentWaitBoundMs` (`src/broker.mjs:2422`), pinned by `demo/mutate-intent-bound.test.mjs`. **One regression was found and closed:** the new
1 s read-drain timer shifted the wake loop by a fraction of a millisecond and
`demo/cooldown-skip-line.test.mjs` went 4/12 red (bisected: 0/12 with `readDrainMs = 0`); it is now driven by an
injected virtual clock and runs 0/15 red in **0.193 s** — pitfall **255**, §F of
`docs/evidence/2026-11-10-cli-signals/ctrl-c-and-read-bounds.md`. Open edges stated there: the first ~270 ms of a
run is still node's default disposition; the force-exit timer cannot fire while a synchronous read blocks the loop
(~2.5 s measured); `tui.mjs` signal behaviour is unmapped; `gcIntentResults` is per-pass, not per read drain — the
architect's exit-drain row **#6391/#6390** (branch `item-6381`, merges clean).
